html:
"Castille" is the map's label, for 1492 and 1500, for the Crown of Castile under Queen Isabella, who ruled it from 1474 to 1504 together with her husband Ferdinand of Aragon.

Their marriage in 1469 joined the two largest Christian kingdoms of the peninsula, though each kept its own laws. Isabella won her throne in a civil war. The couple set up the Spanish Inquisition in 1478 and spent ten years at war with Granada.

1492 was the decisive year. Granada surrendered in January, ending Muslim rule in Iberia. In March the monarchs ordered the expulsion of the Jews. In August Columbus sailed for Castile, and the lands he reached became Castilian. After Isabella died in 1504 Castile passed to her daughter Joanna and then, in 1516, to her grandson Charles, the first king of a united Spain.
